# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 90 (Bi-Vb Pc90)

**ID:** Bi-Vb Pc90
**Section:** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (bi-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 90
**Title (English, from literature):** Getting a massage from a nun
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul7.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 90 (*Bhikkhunī-ummaddāpana*) proscribes a nun from having another nun rub or massage her body, an act classified as an offense of expiation (*pācittiya*) [Hüsken 1997]. Within the Vinaya framework, Pācittiya 90 heads a fourfold sequence of regulations (Pācittiyas 90–93) prohibiting a nun from having herself rubbed or massaged by another nun, a trainee (*sikkhamānā*), a novice (*sāmaṇerī*), or a female householder (*gihinī*) [Cabezón 2017; Hüsken 1997]. Scholarly analysis notes that these rules occupy an intermediate space between monastic hygiene regulations and concerns surrounding physical intimacy, homoerotic behavior, and the inappropriate retention of worldly grooming customs [Cabezón 2017; Hüsken 1997]. Non-offense clauses (*anāpatti*) exempt a nun who receives such rubbing in circumstances of illness, exhaustion resulting from traveling, or distress caused by emergencies such as danger from thieves [Hüsken 1997].

Full parallels to this rule exist across early Buddhist traditions, including the Pali Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha and Parivāra (both Pc 90), as well as Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅgas and Pātimokkhas preserved in Chinese, Tibetan, and Sanskrit belonging to the Dharmaguptaka, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Lokottaravāda, and Sarvāstivāda schools. DharmaNexus records text reuse across 76 Pali texts, showing its closest textual alignments with the subsequent companion rules Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiyas 91–93 (§0.1–2.1.5 ↔ §91.0.1–93.2.1.5), as well as extensive structural formulas shared with Pācittiyas 87, 42, 86, and 84 [DharmaNexus].
